entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 2342 of 2023
Applicant :- Kulveer Singh
Opposite Party :- Central Bureau Of Investigation Anti Corruption Branch Lko.

entities.text: Central Bureau Of Investigation Anti Corruption Branch Lko
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Avinash Tripathi,Dharmendra Kumar Yadav,Mayank Sharma
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Anurag Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.

Heard Sri Mayank Sharma, the learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Dharmendra Pratap Singh, holding brief of Shri Anurag Kumar Singh, the learned counsel for the respondents and perused the records.

2. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in F.I.R. bearing Case Crime No.02 of 2016, R.C. No. RC0062014A0025, under Sections 511 r/w 420 I.P.C.,
registered at Police Station - CBI/ACB/Lucknow, District - Lucknow.

3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 28.08.2014 against 29 named persons, not including the applicant and some unknown persons, stating that in an examination for making selections to 'Group - D' posts in Indian Railways, some imposters had appeared for some candidates.
Kulveer Singh vs Central Bureau Of Investigation Anti ... on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106171075/

entities.text: Kulveer Singh vs Central Bureau Of Investigation Anti
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1 4. The applicant's name is not mentioned in the chargesheet or supplementary chargesheet and his name has surfaced in the second supplementary chargesheet stating that in his place, one Ram Prakash, impersonator had appeared in the written examination.
5.
In the affidavit filed in support of the anticipatory bail-application, it has been stated that the applicant is innocent and he has no criminal history.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant had cooperated with the investigation and thereafter a chargesheet has been filed.
7. The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.

8. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that the examination in question was held in the year 2012-13; the FIR was filed on 28.08.2014 and the applicant's name has come to light in the second supplementary chargesheet, submitted on 29.06.2022; that at this pace, the trial may take take decades to conclude; that the applicant has no criminal history and without making any observations which may affect the outcome of the case, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts are sufficient for making out a case for granting anticipatory bail to the applicant.
9. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
